name: selenium

queries.all: (TITLE_ABS:"selenium" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenomethionine" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenite" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenate") AND SRC:MED
queries.reviews: (TITLE_ABS:"selenium" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenomethionine" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenite" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenate") AND SRC:MED AND (PUB_TYPE:"meta-analysis" OR PUB_TYPE:"systematic review")
queries.trials: (TITLE_ABS:"selenium" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenomethionine" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenite" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenate") AND SRC:MED AND PUB_TYPE:"randomized controlled trial"
queries.guidelines: (TITLE_ABS:"selenium" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenomethionine" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenite" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenate") AND SRC:MED AND PUB_TYPE:"practice guideline"
queries.retracted: (TITLE_ABS:"selenium" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenomethionine" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenite" OR TITLE_ABS:"selenate") AND SRC:MED AND PUB_TYPE:"retracted publication"

rules: Searched every PubMed record in Europe PMC with selenium (selenium, selenomethionine, selenite, selenate) in its title or abstract; downloaded all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
An outcome counts when its words are in the title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of randomised trials of giving selenium, with selenium in the title, or in the abstract of a review of several supplements (not reviews of blood levels in observational studies; reviews without an abstract are kept for screening), and not about another group of people (such as sepsis, intensive care or surgery; each outcome's list is in the search definition). Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most trials pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Screening: each eligible review's title and abstract was read against the finding's question (who, what was given, compared with what, what was measured) by Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only. Only reviews that answer it can be chosen; the others are listed with the reason. The decisions are kept in the repository and have not yet been checked by a clinician.
Overlap: the chosen reviews' reference lists (from Europe PMC) matched against the downloaded selenium trials, measured as the corrected covered area (Pieper 2014, PMID 24581293).

left.title: Vitamin and mineral supplements in the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer: An updated systematic evidence review for the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force

left.title: Selenium for preventing cancer
left.reason: Selenium vs placebo RCTs in adults for cancer, but the RCTs were summarised narratively rather than pooled.

left.title: Selenium and lung cancer: a systematic review and meta analysis
left.reason: Selenium and lung cancer with RCTs, but the abstract shows no pooled RCT estimate and mixes in observational and treatment evidence.

left.title: Systematic review: primary and secondary prevention of gastrointestinal cancers with antioxidant supplements
left.reason: Antioxidant vs placebo RCTs for GI cancers include selenium, but the abstract reports only pooled antioxidant effects.

left.title: The efficacy and safety of multivitamin and mineral supplement use to prevent cancer and chronic disease in adults: a systematic review for a National Institutes of Health state-of-the-science conference
left.reason: Selenium was given only in combination with other vitamins and minerals, with no separate selenium result.

left.title: Intake of selenium in the prevention of prostate cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
left.reason: Only cohort and case-control studies of selenium intake; no randomised trials of supplements.

left.title: Antioxidant supplements for preventing gastrointestinal cancers
left.reason: Antioxidant vs placebo RCTs for GI cancers include selenium, but the abstract shows no separate selenium result.

question.population: Adults without diabetes at the start
question.outcome: New type 2 diabetes, or blood sugar

screening.by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

left.title: Selenium supplementation effect on glycemic control: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
left.reason: Pooled RCTs of selenium vs placebo on fasting blood sugar, but the population is not limited to adults without diabetes.

left.title: Effects of Probiotic and Selenium Co-supplementation on Lipid Profile and Glycemia Indices: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
left.reason: Selenium was always given together with probiotics, so its effect on blood sugar cannot be separated.

left.title: Dietary Supplements Potentially Target Plasma Glutathione Levels to Improve Cardiometabolic Health in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials
left.reason: Covers diabetic patients with glutathione and cardiometabolic outcomes, includes many supplements, and pools no data.

left.title: Potential Benefits of Selenium Supplementation in Reducing Insulin Resistance in Patients with Cardiometabolic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
left.reason: Pooled selenium RCTs on glucose markers, but only in patients with cardiometabolic diseases, so this is treatment rather than prevention.

left.title: Could nutrient supplements provide additional glycemic control in diabetes management? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of as an add-on nutritional supplementation therapy
left.reason: Selenium is one of the add-on supplements studied, but the population is people who already have type 2 diabetes.

left.title: Comparison of nutritional supplements for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized trials
left.reason: Network meta-analysis includes selenium for glycemic markers, but only in adults who already have type 2 diabetes.

left.title: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of exposure to environmental selenium and the risk of type 2 diabetes in nonexperimental studies
left.reason: Pools only observational studies of selenium exposure, not randomised trials of supplements.

left.title: Effectiveness and safety of selenium supplementation for type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults: a systematic review of randomised controlled trials
left.reason: Selenium RCTs on glucose outcomes, but in adults who already have type 2 diabetes (treatment, not prevention).

left.title: The Effects of Selenium Supplementation on Glucose Metabolism and Lipid Profiles Among Patients with Metabolic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
left.reason: Pooled selenium RCTs on fasting glucose and insulin, but only in patients with metabolic diseases.

left.title: Antioxidant agents for delaying diabetic kidney disease progression: A systematic review and meta-analysis
left.reason: Antioxidants for diabetic kidney disease, with kidney outcomes rather than diabetes incidence or blood sugar.
